clinician.trajectory_summary: An 89-year-old female with long-standing stable chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) for >40 years, untreated for 15 years, presented with worsening dyspnea and dry cough following an upper respiratory tract infection treated with azithromycin. Physical examination revealed distress, dyspnea, bibasilar crackles, palpable axillary lymphadenopathies, and sinus tachycardia without fever. Chest X-ray showed enlarged cardiac silhouette, pulmonary congestion, and left lower lobe infiltration. On admission, laboratory studies revealed markedly elevated WBC (67×10³/uL) with mild anemia and thrombocytopenia, mild metabolic acidosis (pH 7.32), and baseline renal function (creatinine 0.76 mg/dL).
